title: POC Workshop Agenda + Acceptance Heuristics — Veridian Insurance
body:
Purpose:
Run a compact, hands-on POC kickoff workshop with Veridian Insurance to validate that Redwood inference can meet their near-real-time claims-triage use case under their operational constraints. Deliverables by end of POC: baseline latency/cost numbers, a minimal integration pattern for secure ingestion, and a pass/fail acceptance scorecard tied to business KPIs.

Scope (what we will do in the POC):
- Integrate a redwood-hosted endpoint with a small claims dataset (anonymized) provided by Veridian.
- Run 3 workload profiles: pilot (10 reqs/s), spike (60 reqs/s burst), and edge-case (long context, 1.5k tokens).
- Validate routing/fallback: primary model -> quantized low-cost fallback under capacity limits.
- Observe token-level cost and per-request latency with tracing enabled.
- Walk through deployment checklist for a Private/VPC option if security gating requires it.

Non-goals (not covered in this sprint):
- Full production rollout, SLA contracts, or multi-region DR.
- Fine-tuning customer models (this POC will use curated open models and Redwood-verified variants).

Attendees (recommended):
- Veridian: Product lead, Claims SME, Network/Security engineer, Compliance owner
- Redwood: Solutions engineer (owner), Platform engineer, Security/Compliance engineer, Customer success manager

Pre-reads (please review before workshop):
- Veridian data redaction checklist (attached)
- Redwood quickstart for hosted endpoints (link: CONFLUENCE-VER-124)
- Short note on model variants and quantization tradeoffs (link: gitlab.com/redwood/ml/notes)

Workshop Agenda (half-day, 4 hours)
- 0:00–0:15 Welcome + objectives + success criteria overview (owner: Arjun Patel)
- 0:15–0:35 Customer context: claims flow, latency expectations, and compliance constraints (Veridian SME)
- 0:35–1:15 Architecture walk: network, data ingress, auth, RBAC, VPC options (Redwood platform eng + Veridian infra)
- 1:15–1:45 Hands-on: register sample pipeline, ingest anonymized claims, quick smoke tests (joint)
- 1:45–2:15 Load profiles: run pilot and spike, observe metrics, validate fallback routing (Redwood SRE + Veridian infra)
- 2:15–2:35 Failure-mode exercise: simulate degraded capacity and observe graceful fallback + alerts
- 2:35–3:00 Acceptance review and scorecard walkthrough; agree on next steps and delivery timeline

Hands-on Exercises (detailed)
- Data ingest: demo pre-ingest redaction script, verify schema mapping and token counts.
- Latency bench: run 1000 short requests, capture p50/p95/p99 and per-token breakdown.
- Cost probe: run steady-state 10 reqs/s for 30 minutes and produce per-1000-token spend estimate.
- Regression check: run sample prompt set to verify output quality (human reviewer) across model variants.

POC Success Heuristics (scorecard)
- Business pass/fail buckets are additive and weighted. Final pass requires >= 75 points.
- Latency (max 40 points): p95 <= 350ms (40 pts), p95 <= 600ms (20 pts), else 0 pts.
- Accuracy / relevancy (max 30 points): human-rated mean relevance >= 4.0/5 across 50 examples (30 pts), 3.5–4.0 (15 pts), else 0 pts.
- Operational integration (max 15 points): secure ingestion via Veridian S3/VPC + token rotation and audit logs in place (15 pts), partial (7 pts), else 0 pts.
- Cost predictability (max 10 points): steady-state spend estimate within 20% of project budget (10 pts), within 50% (5 pts), else 0 pts.
- Failover behavior (max 5 points): automatic fallback to compatible model variant under simulated capacity pressure (5 pts)

Operational Constraints & Must-haves
- Data residency: test runs must use Veridian staging VPC; no raw PII leaves the VPC during the POC.
- Network: egress only allowed via approved IP ranges; mutual TLS for service-to-service.
- Secrets: API keys stored in Veridian KMS; Redwood will demonstrate integration but will not persist secrets post-POC.

Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: Sample set is not representative -> Mitigation: run an additional 25% random sample during final week and re-score.
- Risk: Network policy blocks load testing -> Mitigation: coordinate with Veridian infra to schedule dedicated test window and provide pre-approved IPs.
- Risk: Quality regressions on quantized fallback -> Mitigation: hold manual review and increase beam/temperature heuristics for fallback variant.

Roles & RACI (textual summary)
- Solutions engineer (Redwood): owner of workshop runbook, integration steps, and follow-up artifacts (R)
- Platform engineer (Redwood): supports load tests, observability hooks, and tracing setup (A)
- Veridian product/claims SME: defines acceptance prompts and quality expectations (C)
- Veridian infra/security: approves network/KMS configuration and test windows (A)
- Customer success (Redwood): coordinates logistics, runbooks, and commercial checkpoint at POC end (C)

Delivery timeline (3 weeks recommended)
- Week 0: workshop + baseline runs
- Week 1: focused tuning (routing/quantization) and regression checks
- Week 2: final scorecard runs, cost forecast, and executive summary delivery

Quick checklist (for day 0)
- [ ] Anonymized sample dataset uploaded to staging S3
- [ ] Veridian infra has approved Redwood egress IPs
- [ ] Mutual TLS certs exchanged and tested
- [ ] Tracing and tokenized cost export enabled on Redwood console
- [ ] Acceptance prompt set (50 examples) uploaded and agreed

Open questions (to resolve during planning)
- How large should the spike profile be for downstream systems (beyond Redwood)?
- Does Veridian require encrypted-at-rest logs for request metadata? If so, where is the retention policy defined?
- Are there any rate-limit policies on the staging S3 mount we should be aware of?

Next steps (after workshop)
- Redwood: produce concise POC runbook with exact CLI / API commands and expected artifacts (ETA: 48 hours).
- Veridian: confirm staging dataset and schedule a 2-hour test window for spike testing (ETA: 72 hours).
- Joint: sync on acceptance thresholds and sign off on the final scorecard; set date for executive review.

Notes and context: this doc is intended as a lightweight, actionable kickoff artifact focused on rapid validation rather than a formal contract. Keep it iterative: treatment of any failing heuristic should be a triage item, not an automatic escalation.
